layer: RAG evaluation set (retrieval-gated; generation metrics declared, not measured)

ragas.why: This block describes the `ragas` *library*, which is not installed in this repository or on this machine: installing it would add a dependency tree to a project whose answering path deliberately has none. The four metric definitions it implements — faithfulness, answer relevancy, context precision and context recall — are implemented in `scripts/eval_answer_quality.py` and measured with a judge model in `answer_quality_eval.json`. Those scores are not comparable to a library run, because the prompt, the decomposition and the call pattern are this repository's.

questions.question: What did the published estimate find for the effect of FAAC allocations on reported fatalities?
questions.reference_answer: The published Design A specification is a PPML elasticity of fatalities to the logged gross FAAC allocation of +0.4678 (SE 0.2812), 95 % interval [-0.0833, +1.0189], p = 0.0962, on 3,888 state-months for 36 states from 2016-12 to 2025-12. The interval crosses zero and the verdict is `estimated_not_identified`.

questions.question: Is the fatality estimate identified, and which check decided that?
questions.reference_answer: No. The pre-declared rule requires a lead-shift p-value below 0.05 and a 24-month placebo smaller than the estimate; the lead-shift p-value is 0.167, with 10 of 60 mis-timed doses returning an estimate at least as large as the published one. The verdict is `estimated_not_identified`.

questions.question: What is the point estimate and 95 % interval for the effect on the number of reported incidents?
questions.reference_answer: +0.5278 with a 95 % interval of [+0.1467, +0.9088], p = 0.0066, on the same 3,888 state-months. The interval excludes zero, but the same lead-shift check fails (p = 0.167), so the card still reads `estimated_not_identified`.

questions.question: How much of a Brent crude oil shock reaches state governments, and after how long?
must_contain: cumulative log change in national FAAC
questions.reference_answer: Design B is a local projection of the cumulative log change in national FAAC on the Brent shock. The response is -0.1600 at h = 0, +0.5181 at h = 2 (interval [+0.1919, +0.8443]) and +0.4698 at h = 3, so roughly a 10 % Brent move reaches the states as about 5 % more money two to three months later. Only h = 2 and h = 3 exclude zero.

questions.question: Did Design B's result survive the robustness grid?
questions.reference_answer: Its sign did: 24 of 24 specifications are positive and all 24 intervals exclude zero. Its timing is weaker — the in-time placebo over 48 shifted alignments returns p = 0.0625, published as a bound rather than widened until it passed.

questions.question: Was the synthetic control estimated, and what did its placebos find?
questions.reference_answer: Estimated, and not identified. The donor pool was widened to 99 candidates and the gate passes u5mr on 3 of its 4 runnable windows; the estimator, the in-space and in-time placebos and the leave-one-donor-out sweep were then built. Four windows were estimated and none survived the declared rule: the in-space rank p runs from 0.17 to 0.50, and 304 of 396 placebo fits also clear the same pre-fit gate, so the gate does not discriminate on this pool.

questions.question: Can you show me an estimate for under-5 mortality under the synthetic-control design?
questions.reference_answer: No number appears on the card. The synthetic control was run for under-5 mortality and no window survived its placebos, so the card carries the reason code `design_estimated_not_identified` and points at registry/design_c/ for the gaps, the placebos and the check that failed. A synthetic control has no sampling distribution, so there is no interval to put on a card.

questions.question: How much of the monthly data series is actually observed rather than interpolated?
questions.reference_answer: 1,373 of 8,350 rows are observed (16.4 %); 4,389 are interpolated and 2,588 unobserved. The app draws interpolated months dashed and Stage 7 excludes them on a robustness axis.

questions.question: Why can't you tell me whether PDP or APC tenures did better?
questions.reference_answer: There are four to five administrations against 22–23 annual observations per outcome, and the mandated oil x tenure interactions are collinear with the tenure dummies at R² 0.997–0.999, so the smallest detectable effect is 35–99 residual standard deviations. It is a statement about arithmetic, not a null result.

questions.question: How many of the landed series did the quality gates flag?
questions.reference_answer: 674 series are gated: 359 ok, 313 flagged and 2 empty. A flag means a rule fired and the reason travels with the series; it does not mean the series was removed.

questions.question: How many of the 36 model cards carry a published number?
questions.reference_answer: Two of 36. Both are Design A cards whose outcome Stage 6 published a specification for; the other 34 carry a reason from a closed set, and the two design-level results sit on the index.

questions.question: How can I tell an interpolated value from an observed one in the app?
questions.reference_answer: Every row carries `observation_type`; the app draws `interpolated` segments dashed and Stage 7 excludes them on a robustness axis. Interpolation is linear and only between two observations exactly twelve months apart, and never for a count.

questions.question: Did fatalities change after Buhari was sworn in in 2015, and can that shift be interpreted?
questions.reference_answer: Fatalities fell 67.5 % over the 12 months after the transition (placebo p = 0.017), but the pre-trend placebo moves 83.8 % over the same span, so the cell is `not_interpretable_pre_trend`: the series was already moving that way before the transition.

questions.question: Which period does the COVID-19 shock band cover?
questions.reference_answer: The annotated COVID-19 band runs from 2020-03-01 to 2020-12-01; Brent averaged $18.38 in April 2020. It is a declared annotation on the charts, not a break detected by a test.

questions.question: Who was president in 2012, and for which party?
questions.reference_answer: Goodluck Jonathan (PDP), from 2010-05-06 to 2015-05-29. Acting from 2010-02-09; the sworn-in date is the single decided boundary of the administration spine.

questions.question: What unit is under-5 mortality measured in, and which direction is better?
questions.reference_answer: Per 1,000 live births, annual, and lower is better. The card's coverage status is `partial` because the annual series is largely interpolation across a five-yearly NDHS cycle.

questions.question: Which president had the better record on child mortality?
questions.reference_answer: I don't have a model for that. The tenure comparison needs a counterfactual the data cannot supply: four to five administrations against 22–23 annual observations per national outcome. See docs/limitations.md §1.

questions.question: Can the synthetic control tell me whether Buhari's tenure caused the fall in under-5 mortality?
questions.reference_answer: I don't have a model for that. The synthetic control was run on under-5 mortality, but none of its four windows survived its placebos, so the result is published as estimated_not_identified rather than as an effect of a particular tenure: the in-space rank p runs from 0.17 to 0.50, and 304 of 396 placebo fits clear the same pre-fit gate. See the Design C published result.

questions.question: What will inflation be in 2030?
questions.reference_answer: Refusal. The project holds historical series and published estimates; it makes no forecasts, and no chunk supports one.

questions.question: What was Nigeria's population in 1960?
questions.reference_answer: Refusal. The study window starts in 1999 and the corpus carries no 1960 population figure.

questions.question: How many people live in Kano today?
questions.reference_answer: Refusal. No current sub-national population series is in the corpus (the state population denominator is the unmade decision X-09).

questions.question: Should the federal government increase the FAAC allocation to the states?
questions.reference_answer: Refusal. This is a normative question; the project publishes estimates with intervals and assumptions, not recommendations.
